title: Docs Refresh Editorial Checklist (Streaming + Tools + Structured Output)
content:
Purpose
- This checklist is the “last mile” pass before merging docs-site + SDK guide updates for the Streaming / Tool calling / Structured output refresh.
- Goal: eliminate terminology drift, reduce copy/paste failures, and make troubleshooting discoverable.

How to use
- Run this checklist per page (docs-site) and per snippet location (SDK README, guides, examples repo).
- If a page has multiple language tabs (Python/TypeScript/Go), apply all relevant items to each tab.
- If anything conflicts with the canonical patterns spec, default to the canonical spec and flag in #devex + link the page/PR.


1) Terminology consistency (user-facing)

1.1 Required term choices
- Use “tool calling” (not “function calling”) in headings and primary narrative.
  - Allowed: “(aka function calling)” once per page, preferably in an early note.
- Use “structured output” as the feature name.
  - Avoid “JSON mode” as a headline term; if referenced, treat as legacy phrasing and clarify it maps to structured output.
- Use “streaming” for incremental server-sent events; avoid “realtime tokens” unless as a colloquial aside.

1.2 Canonical nouns (keep exact)
- “stream events” (generic)
- “token delta” (or “text delta” only if the SDK literally labels it that way)
- “tool call delta” for partial tool args/name updates during streaming
- “final response” for the non-streamed, complete object at the end of a stream
- “schema” / “JSON Schema” for structured output constraints
- “validation” for schema validation step; “retry” for the recommended remediation

1.3 Avoid ambiguous language
- Don’t say “the model returns JSON” without specifying:
  - Is it tool call arguments? (tool calling)
  - Is it structured output content constrained by schema? (structured output)
- Don’t say “the stream ends when done” without specifying what the consumer should do with the final event / final response.

1.4 Consistent warnings vocabulary
- Prefer “Warning” for correctness/safety hazards (e.g., partial tool args, insecure tools)
- Prefer “Note” for clarifications (e.g., SDK differences, defaults)
- Prefer “Troubleshooting” for symptom → cause → fix blocks


2) Code block formatting and copy/paste rules

2.1 Language tags and formatting
- Every code block must declare the language (python / ts / javascript / go / bash).
- No “pseudo-code” blocks unless explicitly labeled as pseudo-code and paired with runnable code.
- Keep line length reasonable (target < 100 chars) OR show line breaks that still copy/paste cleanly.

2.2 Minimal runnable requirements
- Snippets must include:
  - Client initialization
  - How API key is read (env var name must be consistent across docs)
  - A single request that demonstrates the feature
  - A “what to print/return” line so users know success criteria
- If the snippet cannot be fully runnable (e.g., tool implementation omitted), it must:
  - Provide a stubbed tool implementation scaffold
  - Explicitly mark “replace with your implementation”

2.3 Environment variables (standardization)
- Use the same env var name across docs and examples (default: REDWOOD_API_KEY).
- If region/base URL is required for private deployments, make it a clearly optional override.
- Do not include real keys, tokens, or customer identifiers.

2.4 Streaming snippets must show the full loop lifecycle
- Must show:
  - Event iteration (for-await/reader loop)
  - Handling token deltas (append to buffer or print)
  - Handling tool call deltas (accumulate in a safe buffer)
  - Handling end-of-stream / final response capture
- Must not imply that each stream event is a complete JSON object for tool args.

2.5 Tool calling snippets: safety baseline
- Must include:
  - Tool allowlist (explicit mapping of tool name → handler)
  - Argument validation (type/shape check) before execution
  - A “default deny” branch for unknown tool names
- Must not include:
  - Shell execution examples (e.g., exec("curl ..."))
  - Unrestricted network calls without clear boundaries
  - Logging raw tool arguments that may contain secrets (unless the example explicitly shows redaction)

2.6 Structured output snippets: schema + validation + retry strategy
- Must include:
  - The schema (inline or clearly imported)
  - Parsing/validation step (e.g., JSON decode + schema validation)
  - A retry strategy on parse/validation failure (at least one retry pattern)
- Must explicitly call out:
  - “Never trust unvalidated JSON”
  - What error users should expect on schema mismatch

2.7 Comments and naming
- Use consistent variable naming across languages when possible:
  - client, stream, event, textBuffer, toolArgsBuffer, finalResponse
- Comments should describe “why” (event semantics, edge cases), not restate the obvious.


3) Narrative + structure checks (per page)

3.1 Page structure expectations
- A reader should be able to answer, within 30 seconds:
  - What feature is this page teaching?
  - Is the example streaming or non-streaming?
  - What should I do with deltas vs the final response?
  - What are the common failure modes?

3.2 Intro paragraph clarity
- Mention the primary use case (e.g., “low latency UI updates”, “reliable tool orchestration”, “guaranteed JSON output shape”).
- State any prerequisites:
  - Required SDK version (if relevant)
  - Any feature flags / headers if applicable

3.3 Avoid overpromises
- Don’t claim schema guarantees without mentioning validation on the client side.
- Don’t claim “tool args are always valid JSON per event” (they are often partial during streaming).

3.4 Callouts must be actionable
- If a Warning exists, it must include a concrete “Do X instead” snippet or bullet.


4) Troubleshooting and reliability guidance

4.1 Required troubleshooting topics to cover (where relevant)
Streaming pages:
- Stream disconnect mid-response
  - Mention common causes: corporate proxies, load balancers, idle timeouts
  - Provide mitigations: keep-alive settings, timeout config, retry/resume guidance (if supported)
- “Final message missing” symptom
  - Clarify the difference between token deltas and final response

Tool calling pages:
- Partial tool arguments during streaming
  - Recommend accumulation + parse only when tool call is complete
  - Recommend JSON parse with clear error handling
- Unknown tool name / tool not allowlisted
  - Show explicit error and safe fallback behavior

Structured output pages:
- Schema mismatch errors after copying older snippets
  - Call out schema versioning / keeping schema in sync
- Silent parse failures
  - Recommend strict parsing + validation and logging of parse errors (with redaction)

4.2 Log guidance must be safe
- If logs are shown, they must redact:
  - API keys, bearer tokens
  - User PII (emails, phone numbers)
  - Full tool arguments if they may contain secrets


5) Cross-link verification (don’t ship broken paths)

5.1 Required links (where applicable)
- “Canonical examples” link must point to redwood-examples and the matching language folder.
- SDK pages must link to SDK reference docs for:
  - streaming API type definitions
  - tool call objects
  - structured output response types
- Troubleshooting callouts should link to the consolidated troubleshooting page (not a Slack thread).

5.2 Validate link integrity
- Click every link in the doc preview (not just in markdown) to catch:
  - bad relative paths after IA changes
  - anchors that no longer exist
  - renamed sections

5.3 IA consistency
- Navigation labels must match page titles (Streaming / Tools / Structured output).
- Ensure quickstarts reference the new section (no “legacy streaming” page links).


6) SDK parity sanity checks (Python / TS / Go)

- Confirm each language tab demonstrates the same conceptual flow:
  - streaming loop → delta handling → tool aggregation → final response
  - structured output → parse → validate → retry
- If a language has a known limitation or different API surface:
  - Add a short “SDK differences” note (one paragraph max)
  - Do not fork the narrative into completely different semantics


7) Snippet test readiness (CI)

- Any snippet intended to be canonical must:
  - Exist in redwood-examples (or be pulled from it)
  - Be runnable in CI with mocked endpoints (no real credentials required)
  - Avoid flaky timing assumptions (sleep-based success checks)
- If a docs-site snippet is intentionally not executed in CI:
  - Mark it as “illustrative” and link to the runnable version


8) Final pre-merge checklist (quick pass)

- Search/replace checks:
  - “function calling” → “tool calling” (unless “aka function calling” once)
  - “json mode” → “structured output” (with legacy mention if needed)
- No references to removed/legacy event names.
- All code blocks render correctly (no broken fences, correct indentation).
- No internal-only links on public docs pages (Confluence, Linear, Jira).
- Confirm warnings exist for:
  - partial tool args
  - schema validation
  - safe tool execution


Notes / open issues (keep short)
- If you find a recurring pattern problem, add it here and ping #devex so we can bake it into the canonical examples and snippet tests.

Change log
- 2026-01-19: Initial checklist draft (Elliot)
- 2026-01-27: Added tool safety and structured output retry requirements (Marcus review)
- 2026-02-10: Finalized terminology mapping + cross-link rules after IA updates (docs PR_904)
